sequence_description: SAML brokered login: attempt to authenticate with a SAMLResponse where the Response is signed but the Assertion is not individually signed (classic signature-wrapping/partial-signature acceptance).
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML login succeeded with an unsigned Assertion (only the Response envelope signed), indicating acceptance of partial-signature SAMLResponses and potential signature-wrapping risk.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML login succeeded with an unsigned Assertion (only the Response envelope signed), indicating acceptance of partial-signature SAMLResponses and potential signature-wrapping risk.

sequence_description: OIDC SSO brokered login: attempt to authenticate with an ID token that uses attacker-controlled 'kid' to select an untrusted key (kid injection / key confusion). Broker must reject if it verifies against the wrong key or accepts attacker-signed tokens.
description: [LLM-Judge] OIDC/SAML broker accepted an attacker-minted JWT with attacker-controlled 'kid', resulting in account/claim impersonation (victim email) instead of rejecting untrusted key material.

evidence.llm_judge_description: OIDC/SAML broker accepted an attacker-minted JWT with attacker-controlled 'kid', resulting in account/claim impersonation (victim email) instead of rejecting untrusted key material.

sequence_description: Direct endpoint attack: attempt client_credentials login using a JWT with alg=none semantics (unsigned token). Control: obtain a normal M2M token first to ensure setup is correct, then attempt alg=none token acceptance.
description: [LLM-Judge] The platform returned HTTP 200/success for a login attempt using a purported 'alg=none' JWT attack token, suggesting the token may have been accepted (or the test did not actually mint an alg=none token).

evidence.llm_judge_description: The platform returned HTTP 200/success for a login attempt using a purported 'alg=none' JWT attack token, suggesting the token may have been accepted (or the test did not actually mint an alg=none token).

sequence_description: Direct endpoint attack: attempt client_credentials login using a JWT with alg=none semantics (unsigned token). Control: obtain a normal M2M token first to ensure setup is correct, then attempt alg=none token acceptance.
description: [LLM-Judge] Both the control and attack flows produced tokens that introspect as inactive, indicating introspection is not validating/recognizing these tokens or the wrong token type is being introspected, undermining the test’s ability to confirm rejection/acceptance.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Both the control and attack flows produced tokens that introspect as inactive, indicating introspection is not validating/recognizing these tokens or the wrong token type is being introspected, undermining the test’s ability to confirm rejection/acceptance.

sequence_description: Direct endpoint attack: attempt client_credentials login using a JWT with alg=none semantics (unsigned token). Control: obtain a normal M2M token first to ensure setup is correct, then attempt alg=none token acceptance.
description: [LLM-Judge] The minted 'alg_none' token header shows RS256 (signed) rather than alg=none, so the test artifact does not match the intended unsigned-JWT attack and any acceptance result is inconclusive.

evidence.llm_judge_description: The minted 'alg_none' token header shows RS256 (signed) rather than alg=none, so the test artifact does not match the intended unsigned-JWT attack and any acceptance result is inconclusive.

sequence_description: Brokered SAML login: attempt to authenticate using a forged SAMLResponse signed with attacker cert (untrusted signing key). Broker must reject if it properly validates SAML signature trust anchor.
description: [LLM-Judge] Forged SAML login attempt failed due to missing/invalid SSO connector resolution (session.invalid_connector_id) rather than an explicit SAML signature trust validation failure, so the test did not actually exercise attacker-signed assertion rejection.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Forged SAML login attempt failed due to missing/invalid SSO connector resolution (session.invalid_connector_id) rather than an explicit SAML signature trust validation failure, so the test did not actually exercise attacker-signed assertion rejection.

sequence_description: SAML SSO: include OneTimeUse and reuse the same Assertion/@ID across two logins to test replay detection.
description: [LLM-Judge] Replay attempt failed, but error indicates missing/invalid SAML connector ID rather than explicit OneTimeUse/Assertion ID replay detection, so replay protection behavior is not actually validated.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Replay attempt failed, but error indicates missing/invalid SAML connector ID rather than explicit OneTimeUse/Assertion ID replay detection, so replay protection behavior is not actually validated.

sequence_description: OIDC SSO nonce freshness enforcement: attempt brokered OIDC SSO login where the RP expects nonce binding but the mock IdP omits nonce in id_token. The RP must reject. Include a second identity via password login as control evidence that the system is otherwise functional.
description: [LLM-Judge] OIDC SSO login succeeded even though the IdP omitted the nonce in the id_token, indicating missing/incorrect nonce freshness enforcement (nonce bypass).

evidence.llm_judge_description: OIDC SSO login succeeded even though the IdP omitted the nonce in the id_token, indicating missing/incorrect nonce freshness enforcement (nonce bypass).

sequence_description: OIDC flow coherence: attempt to splice an authorization code from session A into session B by exchanging it under a different client_id (cross-client code injection).
description: [LLM-Judge] Identity verification captured a display_name despite no authenticated session token, suggesting possible state leakage or incorrect binding of identity attributes to an unauthenticated context.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Identity verification captured a display_name despite no authenticated session token, suggesting possible state leakage or incorrect binding of identity attributes to an unauthenticated context.

sequence_description: I4 attack: attempt account takeover by logging in via OIDC SSO with email_verified=false but victim's email; platform must not map attacker principal to victim identity.
description: [LLM-Judge] SSO login created/returned a different principal for the same email/display name as an existing local user, indicating potentially unsafe account linking behavior (should not link when email_verified=false, and should have clear collision handling).

evidence.llm_judge_description: SSO login created/returned a different principal for the same email/display name as an existing local user, indicating potentially unsafe account linking behavior (should not link when email_verified=false, and should have clear collision handling).

sequence_description: Empty/degenerate upstream principal attack: attempt two OIDC SSO logins with different emails but empty sub to see if broker collapses them into one identity (principal binding should not treat empty sub as a stable identifier).
description: [LLM-Judge] SSO logins with an empty/degenerate upstream principal identifier appear to be accepted and mapped to the same broker user, indicating the broker may be treating an empty subject as a stable identifier (risk of account collision/impersonation if other claims vary).

evidence.llm_judge_description: SSO logins with an empty/degenerate upstream principal identifier appear to be accepted and mapped to the same broker user, indicating the broker may be treating an empty subject as a stable identifier (risk of account collision/impersonation if other claims vary).

sequence_description: Cross-protocol identity merge probe: create two local users, then SSO-login with email_verified=true matching one local user's email but with a different upstream sub; verify broker does not collapse distinct principals into the wrong downstream subject.
description: [LLM-Judge] Account takeover via cross-protocol identity merge: SAML SSO login with email_verified=true was mapped to an existing local user solely by matching email, collapsing distinct principals into the victim’s downstream subject.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Account takeover via cross-protocol identity merge: SAML SSO login with email_verified=true was mapped to an existing local user solely by matching email, collapsing distinct principals into the victim’s downstream subject.

sequence_description: OIDC SSO: attempt principal collision via sub case-folding (sub='Alice' vs sub='alice') while keeping email distinct to avoid by-design email linking.
description: [LLM-Judge] OIDC/SAML SSO login created/linked identities that inherited an existing local user's display name (user_B) despite distinct emails, indicating account confusion/impersonation via principal collision (case-folding of subject).

evidence.llm_judge_description: OIDC/SAML SSO login created/linked identities that inherited an existing local user's display name (user_B) despite distinct emails, indicating account confusion/impersonation via principal collision (case-folding of subject).

sequence_description: SAML: attempt identity collision by keeping NameID constant but changing Issuer (idp_entity_id) across logins; distinct IdPs should not collapse into one subject unless explicitly configured.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML logins from two different Issuers appear to resolve to the same internal subject (identity_id/entity_id), suggesting possible issuer confusion or IdP separation not being enforced.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML logins from two different Issuers appear to resolve to the same internal subject (identity_id/entity_id), suggesting possible issuer confusion or IdP separation not being enforced.

sequence_description: Probe whether a SAML assertion missing Conditions is accepted and yields a usable session token for an API resource (authorization binding should not be broadened by accepting unconstrained assertions).
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML login appears to succeed and yields an active OIDC session/token even though the assertion is described as missing the SAML Conditions element (potential acceptance of unconstrained assertions).

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML login appears to succeed and yields an active OIDC session/token even though the assertion is described as missing the SAML Conditions element (potential acceptance of unconstrained assertions).
